USU unilat - purulent d/c at lid margins & corners of eye reappears w.in min of wiping (vs viral → pus ⍉appear spont & cont)
Conjunctival injection w drainage - minimal if any eyelid or periorbital involvement (vs preseptal cellulitis)
S. aureus common - purulent d/c w.o viral prodrome
Clin - fluorescein staining to look for keratitis or corneal abrasions
bulbar conjunctiva covers globe · tarsal conjunctiva covers eyelids
•adenovirus types 8 · 19 & 37 → epidemic keratoconjunctivitis (↓vision ← corneal subepithelial infiltrate) - types 3 · 4 · 7 & 11 → pharyngitis · fever · malaise · preauricular LAD
FB or gritty sensation · ocular erythema · itching - norm vision
watery or mucopurulent d/c · burning or sandy sensation · morning crusting → daytime watery d/c
Often starts unilat → bilat after 1-2d (may stay unilat w HSV)
+/- viral sxs (viral prodrome → URI · pharyngitis · LAD · fever)
•follicular (bumpy) appearing tarsal conjunctivae · enlrg & tender preauricular LN
•conjunctiva (norm transparent) vascularized w sm vessels → pink or red - watery d/c ± scant mucus
•chemosis ⍉common - red flag for more serious conditions (hyperacute bact conjunctivitis · orbital cellulitis)

ddx blepharitis: irritation · burning & itching of eyelid margin - anterior → scales or collarettes clinging to lashes - posterior → hyperemic lid margins w telangiectasia · inflam meibomian glands & orifices
Dx of exclusion - only in pts w norm vision after keratitis · iritis & acute angle-closure glaucoma r/o
red flags (⍉simple conjunctivitis): ↓visual acuity · ciliary flush · photophobia · corneal opacity · fixed pupil · severe HA w nausea - consider corneal FB · corneal abrasion
- warm to cool compresses · artificial tears · antihist · decongestants
•HSV conjunctivitis → topical ganciclovir 0.15% + systemic antiviral (acyclovir · valacyclovir)
•abx drops ⍉indicated (may prevent 2° bact infect) - many daycares & schools require 24hrs of topical abx b4 return (highly contagious)
•contact lens wearers: anti-pseudomonal abx drops (↑risk Pseudomonas keratitis) · d/c lenses until tx complete → new pair
Inflam of the conjunctiva in response to an allergen
: contact of airborne allergen w eye (w specific IgE) → mast cell degranulation & his release
Type I IgE-mediated hypersensitivity - mediators: his (main early response → itching & vasopermeability) · eos · basophils · neutrophils (late response · often 6-10hrs → characteristic inflam)
RF: atopic asthma · atopic derm · allergic rhinitis
•acute: sudden rxn to known enviro allergen (cat dander) - intense itching · hyperemia · tearing · chemosis · eyelid edema - USU resolves w.in 24hrs once exposure ends
•seasonal: assoc w rhinitis - outdoor airborne pollen (weeds · grasses · trees) - similar sx but develop gradually (over days) & less intense
•perennial: mild waxing & waning - year-round indoor allergens (dust mites · animal dander · mold)
Other allergic sxs: nasal congestion · sneezing ·
Bilat - may have follicular tarsal conjunctivae & profuse watery d/c like viral - itching + Hx of allergy or hay fever = diff vs viral
Ocular itching in all types - ⍉itching → consider other dx - stringy d/c · occasional photophobia · eye pain USU absent
⍉fever (hypersensitivity ⍉infect) · ⍉preauricular LAD (vs viral → tender preauricular LN) · ⍉vision loss

•supportive (cool compresses · artificial tears) · allergen avoidance · topical or PO antihist · mast cell stabilizers
•dual-action (antihist + mast cell stabilizer) in peds: olopatadine 0.1% · 0.2% · 0.7% · alcaftadine 0.25% · ketotifen 0.025%
Neonatal conjunctival infect contracted by newborns during delivery
Gonococcal (N. gonorrhoeae): eyes MC affected site in newborns - transmitted via contact during vaginal delivery
RF: sexually active adults · vaginal birth to mother infected w N. gonorrhoeae
•untx → spread to subconjunctival tissue & cornea → corneal ulceration · scarring · ↓vision or blindness
•mild swelling w watery d/c → mucopurulent · severe eyelid swelling w chemosis · pseudomembrane on orbital surface · bloody d/c ← friable conjunctiva
Gonococcal: gram stain & cx of ocular d/c → gram (-) intracell diplococci - grow on modified Thayer-Martin agar
•coinfection w C. trachomatis common → also test - swab of everted eyelid for conjunctival epithelial cells (ocular d/c ⍉appropriate specimen)
•NAAT - more cost-effective & faster for gonococcal & chlamydial conjunctivitis

•Chlamydia: sus exposure (untx maternal infect or ⍉prenatal care) → conjunctival & nasopharyngeal swabs - NAAT gold strd (cx = expensive & time-intensive) - test all for N. gonorrhoeae - tx gonorrhea only if confirmed
•Strd neonatal prophylaxis against gonococcal conjunctivitis given STAT after birth =
•topical erythromycin or silver nitrate prophylaxis → primarily vs N. gonorrhoeae
•only for prophylaxis in newborns at ↑risk - inadeq for tx of active gonococcal infect
•⍉PO azithro as prophylaxis (unnecessary systemic med) · ⍉IM ceftriaxone (tx only) · ⍉topical acyclovir (HSV lesions only)
•tx of mother b4 delivery = most effective prev of bact conjunctivitis - preg pts w PID ← N. gonorrhoeae → admit for IV cefoxitin or cefotetan + azithro 1g PO single dose
may be helpful once it occurs
•admit · r/o disseminated dz (sepsis · arthritis · meningitis) · r/o & tx poss C. trachomatis coinfection
•ceftriaxone 25-50mg/kg IV or IM (max 125mg) - ⍉if receiving Ca-containing IVF or clin sig hyperbilirubinemia
•eval & tx mother & sexual partners for STIs
•<2wks old: erythromycin assoc w infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis → monitor for signs of intestinal obstruct
